images.title: Two screws, one tiny difference
images.purpose: Show two screws that look the same at a glance but differ slightly in length, raising the need for a smaller unit.
images.composition: Two screws lie side by side, one above the other, centred with wide white space; the tiny extra length is the only highlighted detail.
exact_structure: Two horizontal screws, same thickness, same thread style, drawn flat with thin dark outlines, stacked one above the other with their left ends aligned.
Top screw is teal (#0072B2), labelled Screw A. Bottom screw is amber (#E69F00), labelled Screw B and slightly longer than A (about 6 percent longer).
A thin dashed grey (#6B7280) vertical line drops from the right tip of Screw A through Screw B, so the small extra piece of Screw B beyond it is visible.
The small extra piece of Screw B beyond the dashed line is filled reddish purple (#CC79A7).
A small question label sits to the right of the extra piece. No ruler, no numbers.
rejection: the two screws differ by an obvious large amount instead of a tiny one
any number or ruler marks drawn
any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Two things can look the same and still differ by a small amount we cannot yet name.
images.description: Two screws aligned at the left, the lower one slightly longer, with the small extra piece highlighted.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to spot the difference first, then to say what they would need to measure it.

image_decisions.why: The hook shows the story objects simply and poses the question that the rest of the topic answers.
